summary: On 29 May 2026, OpenAI reported degraded login and account creation affecting both the API login and ChatGPT login components. OpenAI began investigating at 03:12, applied mitigation at 03:28 and declared all impacted services fully recovered at 04:57, a 105-minute public incident window. The provider did not disclose a technical root cause, affected-user count or regional distribution.

assessment_boundaries: The public status evidence establishes service state and timing but does not disclose the technical root cause, affected-user count or regional distribution.
No access-state collapse, authentication-transition propagation or verification-dependency mechanism is inferred from login and account-creation symptoms alone.
The separate same-day ChatGPT access incident remains a distinct record because no shared root cause is established.
vigil_assessment.factual_basis: OpenAI's first-party incident page reports issues logging in or creating accounts, with affected components identified as API Login and ChatGPT Login. The provider began investigating at 03:12 on 2026-05-29, reported that mitigation had been applied at 03:28 and declared full recovery at 04:57. The public record therefore establishes a 105-minute authentication and registration availability incident, but it does not identify the technical cause or quantify affected users. The 105-minute interval is the public investigation-to-resolution window; the page supplies no independent onset time or timezone.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The evidenced boundary is service availability, not authority state. A login symptom does not establish that expired, suspended, restricted, unavailable or revoked states were conflated; that an authentication transition failed to propagate; or that an otherwise valid entitlement depended on a verifier that could not complete. The provider's distinct investigating, monitoring and resolved updates preserved a usable operational recovery state, while the undisclosed cause prevents a more specific mechanism adjudication. The material episodes retain resolved-no-mapping dispositions. The occurrence is fully adjudicated but unclassified, which does not assert that every invariant held. Clear operational status updates and recovery do not establish all recognition conditions of an access-state success. No reviewed FC-derived candidate or independently source-identified admitted external requirement is established here; no external compliance finding is implied. Independent occurrence-level external assessment finds affirmative, source-bounded repair in the reported restoration stage. Relevant communication/incident-process requirements remain Boundary where the decisive plan or implementation record is not public. Requirements addressing a different technical object, lifecycle or source date remain audit-only; voluntary adoption is not a gate.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: This incident shows why VIGIL separates occurrence evidence from mechanism inference. Status reporting can establish affected surfaces, duration and recovery while remaining insufficient to determine which internal governance boundary failed. CAM analysis should preserve that uncertainty and require more detailed causal evidence before assigning access-state, session-continuity or verification-dependency controls.
